about: Every attribution the head census of step measure found in the 1841-45 printing (forms read alike in both copies, and forms read in one copy only where they name a writer), and CCEL's head forms for Matthew and Mark, each mapped to a writer only where the printed form, the edition's own Table or the margins name him; otherwise served as printed and never guessed. Pseudo- authors stay distinct. Dates are read from the Catholic Encyclopedia (Robert Appleton, 1907-12) as the golden is read: the article opening’s OCR (archive.org) copied by code with place phrases trimmed, checked by eye against the page image named in page_image, and every difference listed in ocr_corrections; birth and death are stored as printed, or left out with the reason. Greek or Latin is given only where the article states it, with the phrase and its page image; otherwise ‘not stated’. Unresolved printed forms carry their candidate articles but no dates.
later_writer_rule: a later writer: the Catholic Encyclopedia, "Fathers of the Church" (vol. VI, 1909), says the Fathers include in the West Gregory the Great (d. 604) and in the East John Damascene (d. about 754), who "closes the patristic period"; this writer died after that
